title: Being universally closed descends along fpqc coverings (Stacks 02KS)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For $i\in I$ let $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ be the base change of $f$ along $g_i$, the second projection of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f_i$ is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism] (for every morphism $T\to S_i$ the base change $(X\times_SS_i)\times_{S_i}T\to T$ is a closed map of underlying topological spaces) for every $i\in I$, then $f$ is universally closed.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KS (lemma-descending-property-universally-closed, line 5515: 'The property P(f) = "f is universally closed" is fpqc local on the base'), the direction 'each base change $X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ has the property $\Rightarrow$ $f$ has it' of Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310); proof lines 5520-5563 (via Lemma Tag 02KP and Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02JY lemma-fpqc-quotient-topology)

proof.text: *Condition (0), invariance under isomorphism.* Universal closedness is transported across an isomorphism of the source and target morphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-isomorphism], which is the declaration `universallyClosed_respectsIso`.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KS via the condition (0) convention in Definition Tag 02KO (property invariant under isomorphism)

proof.text: *Condition (1), stability under flat base change.* In fact universal closedness is stable under arbitrary base change, so it is stable under a flat base change by [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-base-change].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KS (lemma-descending-property-universally-closed), proof, first sentence: 'A base change of a universally closed morphism is universally closed by definition', condition (1) of Lemma Tag 02KP

proof.text: *Condition (2), Zariski locality on the base.* If the target is covered by open subschemes and the restrictions of a morphism to those opens are universally closed, then the morphism is universally closed by [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-zariski-local].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02K7 (lemma-universally-closed-local-on-the-base), as cited in the proof of Descent Tag 02KS for condition (2) of Tag 02KP

proof.text: *Condition (3), the affine faithfully flat case.* Let $S$ and $S'$ be affine, let $g:S'\to S$ be flat and surjective, and let $f:X\to S$ have universally closed base change along $g$. The morphism $g$ is affine because both its source and target are affine, hence it is quasi-compact. Therefore the Mathlib instance `descendsAlong_universallyClosed_surjective_inf_flat_inf_quasicompact` specializes to [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-affine-descent] and gives that $f$ is universally closed.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KS proof in the affine case, through the general criterion Tag 02KP (flat surjective morphism of affine schemes)

proof.text: *Conclusion by the fpqc-local criterion.* Conditions (0)-(3) above are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-local-on-base-criterion] for the class of universally closed morphisms. Applying that criterion to $f:X\to S$ and the given fpqc covering $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}$, whose base changes $f_i$ are universally closed by hypothesis, proves that $f$ is universally closed.
